messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High DNS error rate detected on azure-koreasouth private-peering -> metric: dns_failure_rate > 8% over 1m. Affected: Dedicated clusters (koreasouth), some Private VPC traffic to on-prem tenants. Severity: P1. Incident ID INC-2478901
SRE-Leah: seeing this on dashboards. KV cache misses, heavy dns NXDOMAINs from our rediscovery service.
SRE-Leah: rolling tail logs now, giving samples.
oncall-azure: I'm on it, digging into ExpressRoute path and VPN handoffs.
Network-Nate: can you paste the traceroute from an impacted node? I want to see if traffic is going to MSFT private nexthop or being blackholed.
SRE-Leah: traceroute sample:
```
traceroute to 10.10.40.1 (10.10.40.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.240.0.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  192.168.200.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  * * *
```
SRE-Leah: lots of * from hop 3.
Platform-Sam: confirm impact: Are customer API calls failing or just elevated latency? Any 5xx counts?
SRE-Leah: both. 5xx spike on control plane for provisioning and a ~4% increase in request errors for live inference. Some customers reporting model timeout.
CS-Maya: Got two on-prem customers on koreasouth reporting degraded throughput. They're asking for ETA.
incident-bot: Related alerts: DNS resolver error rate (azure-koreasouth) = 12% (1m), BGP session flaps noticed on vnet-peering-1 (3 flaps in 10m).
oncall-azure: I opened a ticket with Azure support (SR# 2026-AZ-KS-8892) and requested urgent network control-plane check. They acknowledged.
Network-Nate: temp mitigation idea: move affected customer routes to koreacentral or use public egress for control plane until MSFT fixes. Can we shift only control-plane endpoints?
Platform-Sam: we can reroute provisioning/control-plane traffic for a subset via koreacentral lambda of the router config. Need to update routing policy and NGW routes. Risk: route change might cause auth token source-IP mismatch for some customers.
Eng-Runbook: checklist: 1) confirm impacted customer list, 2) create temporary route policy, 3) throttle background jobs, 4) notify customers.
SRE-Leah: doing step 1 now. Customer impact tags: tier-1 dedicated (3 clusters), 5 small private clusters, 2 enterprise on-prem customers.
Platform-Sam: I'll prepare the route change. Posting command snippet below (do not run without ack):
```
az network route-table route create --resource-group RG-EG --route-table-name rt-egress --name reroute-to-koreacentral --address-prefix 0.0.0.0/0 --next-hop-type VirtualAppliance --next-hop-ip-address 10.50.1.4
```
Network-Nate: we should also add a DNS resolver fallback to public 8.8.8.8 for control-plane only. Quick test shows it reduces failures for probes.
SRE-Leah: quick A/B test: switching control-plane DNS to 8.8.4.4 for one test-node -> errors drop to baseline.
CS-Maya: telling affected customers we're doing an emergency mitigation and will follow up. No ETA yet.
Platform-Sam: proceeding with staged reroute for non-critical clusters first. I'll run change at +2m after posting.
SRE-Leah: applying throttles to background sync jobs now to limit additional DNS load.
oncall-azure: Azure says they're seeing elevated control-plane DNS resolution times within koreasouth and are investigating an internal resolver cluster. They suggested our mitigation (use alternate resolver).
incident-bot: Change log: reroute task started by Platform-Sam at 2478901270; DNS fallback applied for test node at 2478901276.
SRE-Leah: test-node now stable. Control-plane errors reduced from 6% -> 0.9%. Pushing fallback to tier-1 clusters now.
Network-Nate: implementing DNS fallback at scale: pushing systemd-resolved override to resolver-daemonset for private clusters. Rolling update strategy: 10% pods at a time.
Eng-Runbook: note to oncall: once Azure confirms fix, revert DNS overrides and routes, and run a postmortem.
Platform-Sam: reroute completed for non-critical clusters. Will schedule tier-1 after CS-Maya acknowledgement.
CS-Maya: tier-1 customers want phone updates. I'm coordinating with Customer Success to call them in 10m.
SRE-Leah: traffic metrics show recovery trend. Errors down to 1.2% cluster-wide.
oncall-azure: Azure updated SR: "Investigating internal DNS resolver backend in koreasouth; potential cache stampede due to recent prefix redistribution. Engineers working on cache warmup and rolling restart."
Network-Nate: sounds like resolver cluster had a cache eviction/regen event. Our fallback was correct.
SRE-Leah: preparing incident summary for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = Azure resolver instability leading to NXDOMAINs and control-plane errors; contributing factor = high DNS QPS after recent deployment causing thundering herd on resolver cluster.
incident-bot: Paging: Next oncall rotation (oncall-azure) assigned to SRE-Leah for handoff at 2478901320.
Platform-Sam: handing off to oncall-azure. I'll remain available.
oncall-azure: taking over. Will keep SR open and coordinate with Azure until we get confirmation of full resolution.
CS-Maya: flags: two enterprise customers requested incident bridge. Setting up bridge and sending invites now.
SRE-Leah: will collect logs+pcaps for postmortem and upload to the incident folder.
Platform-Sam: postmortem action items I can start: 1) Add DNS-fallback playbook, 2) Add automatic route failover option for ExpressRoute, 3) Add alert for resolver cache regen events.
Eng-Runbook: good. Also add customer-visible mitigation notes for CS.
SRE-Leah: last check: metrics stable and Azure confirms resolver restarts succeeded in koreasouth. I'll mark the incident as mitigated but keep it active until SR is resolved.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2478901 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
oncall-azure: updating SR with our mitigation details and asking for RCA ETA.
CS-Maya: customers briefed. One wants SLA credit estimate; finance/sales looped.
SRE-Leah: closing notes: if anyone sees relapse, ping this thread and we escalate.
Platform-Sam: thanks all. :heart:
